data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella boat rental for April 2034? Easter weekend (2–5 April 2034) offers mild weather, light winds, and uncrowded waters – ideal for a day on the Mediterranean. This guide covers what to expect from the weather, which boats suit your group, and how to lock in the best dates. Sea temperatures hover around 18°C, air temps reach 22°C, and sunshine lasts 8–9 hours daily. Whether you’re after a family cruise or a luxury party, April delivers reliable conditions for a memorable charter from Puerto Banús.

April 2034 Weather Overview for Marbella

April in Marbella sits between spring and early summer. Average daytime highs of 20–22°C and lows of 14–16°C make for comfortable cruising. The sea temperature averages 18°C – cool but swimmable. Winds typically blow from the west or southwest at 10–15 knots, rarely exceeding 20 knots. Easter weekend often sees stable high pressure, with minimal rain (only 3–4 rainy days on average for the month). UV levels are moderate (index 5–6), so bring sunscreen. Visibility at sea is excellent, often exceeding 10 nautical miles.

Easter Weekend 2034: Key Dates and Conditions

Easter 2034 runs from Good Friday (2 April) to Easter Monday (5 April). Historically, this period enjoys settled weather. Expect morning temperatures of 16°C rising to 22°C by midday. Sea breezes pick up around 11am, perfect for sailing. Afternoon clouds are rare. Sunset is around 8:30pm, giving you long daylight hours for a full-day charter (8 hours). If you prefer a shorter trip, half-day charters (4 hours) are also available – the Mangusta 80 at €4,719 for 4 hours includes a free jet ski.

Which Boat to Choose for April Charters

Small groups (up to 5 pax) suit the Dubhe (8m) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m) – both nimble and fuel-efficient. For 8–10 guests, the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 are excellent value at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours (skipper, drinks, and VAT included). Larger parties (12 pax) can opt for the Mangusta 80 (white or grey) at €4,719 minimum 4 hours, or the luxurious Ferretti 94 (29m) and Canados 86 (26m) – pricing on request via WhatsApp. All depart from Puerto Banús and include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and refreshments.

Best Routes for an April Boat Trip

From Puerto Banús, head east to Cabopino (20 minutes) – a quiet cove with golden sand and calm waters. Or go west to Estepona (30 minutes) for a charming marina and beachside restaurants. For more seclusion, Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés offer sheltered anchorages. The coast is less crowded than in June–August, so you’ll enjoy more privacy. If you have a full day, push further to Sotogrande (45 minutes) for a luxurious stop. All routes benefit from light winds and stable conditions in April.

What’s Included in Your Charter

Every boat rental includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Onboard, you’ll find water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. No hidden costs – just turn up at Puerto Banús with your swimwear and sunscreen. For the Mangusta 80, a jet ski is included free for the first 4 hours. Larger yachts like the Ferretti 94 and Canados 86 can be customised with catering or extra water toys – just ask via WhatsApp.

Booking Tips for Easter Weekend 2034

Easter is a peak period. Book at least 4 weeks ahead, ideally 6–8 weeks, to secure your preferred boat. The Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 are popular for their value. The Mangusta 80 (both white and grey) fills quickly for the jet ski offer. For groups of 12, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) and Maiora 26m (26m) are excellent choices.
